narrative.overview:
Parallel translates the tactile precision of a Swiss editing room and physical film light table into a fast, zero-account browser reference board. Most video tools default to heavy dark-slate toolbars that smother footage or generic social feeds full of chrome. Parallel flips the dynamic: at rest, the board is a crisp, archival off-white light table (paper-canvas) ruled in deep carbon ink (carbon-ink) so 50 to 200+ heterogeneous video clips sit side-by-side with zero visual friction.

Playfulness lives in kinetic feedback rather than decoration. Borrowing the red "on-air" tally light from broadcast monitors and the crisp click of hardware transport keys, a single Tally Red (tally-red) accent wakes up only when the user engages: hovering a clip illuminates its frame, flips on a live 2x tally pill, and runs a 3px progress hairline along the bottom edge. Because only one clip plays at a time, the red tally becomes a moving spotlight that follows the user's eye across the grid. Clicking any clip dims the workspace into an Obsidian Screening Room (screening-black) for distraction-free 1x playback with audio.
keyCharacteristics: Videos are the interface: Compact 104px combined top chrome puts playable footage in the first viewport immediately.
Minimal at rest, playful in motion: Quiet neutral surfaces pair with tactile pill buttons, crisp ink lips, and an unmistakable red 2x tally state.
Two-room contrast: Archival light-table browsing (#F6F5F2) transitions cleanly into an obsidian cinema lightbox (#0E0E10) on click.
Accessible by structure: High-contrast ink-on-paper typography, tabular monospace indicators, visible focus rings, and touch-first mobile fallbacks.

rules.name: The 85/12/3 Tally Rule
rules.body: Keep 85% of every viewport in light-table neutrals, 12% in Carbon Ink for text and active pills, and at most 3% in Tally Red. Red's rarity is what makes the single active 2x clip jump off the grid instantly.

rules.name: The Two-Room Rule
rules.body: Never mix dark cinema chrome into the light-table grid, and never open a white modal over a playing 1x video. Browsing belongs on paper-canvas; sound-on inspection belongs in screening-black.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Every counter, playback rate (2x, 1x), and timecode uses JetBrains Mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so numbers never shift width when filters or loops update.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Video cards carry zero drop shadow at rest. Elevation appears only on the single active hovered card or modal overlays, keeping a 200-clip grid visually calm and GPU-light.

dos: Do keep video frames completely free of permanent text overlays, dark gradients, or player controls at rest so clips lead from pixel one.
Do enforce single-active 2x hover playback with Tally Red (#D91E18) border, 2x badge, and 3px progress hairline—and immediately reset currentTime = 0 on pointer leave.
Do rely on native <video preload="metadata"> gated by IntersectionObserver for thumbnails instead of <canvas> frame extraction.
Do isolate broken or unplayable video URLs inside removable dashed red error tiles without interrupting neighboring clips.
Do maintain a 44px x 44px minimum touch target on mobile controls and show the resting play indicator on @media (hover: none) devices.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: reduce by removing hover lifts and badge spring animations while keeping explicit 2x/1x video playback intact.
donts: Don't add a marketing hero section, login button, search bar, or multi-select filter drawer above the board in v1.
Don't flood large backgrounds or card surfaces with Tally Red—keep red under 3% of the viewport so active states stay unmistakable.
Don't use blurry SaaS drop shadows on resting grid cards or rounded 24px+ corners that crop into video corners.
Don't open a white modal for 1x video playback; always transition into the obsidian screening-black (#0E0E10) screening room.
Don't require hover to inspect clips on touch devices; tapping any card on mobile must open the lightbox immediately.
